column2: The Big Dipper (seven stars of 北斗) arcing across the icon as a glowing golden constellation, its third star (天璣) blazing much brighter than the others with a radiant cross-shaped flare, all seven stars joined by luminous gold threads; behind them a faint golden halo ring and a swirl of deep blue nebula. Majestic and simple.

A taiji (yin-yang) disc formed by two swirling nebulae, one of molten gold light and one of deep indigo-violet starry space, spiralling into each other; the two eye dots are a bright gold star and a dark blue star. Thin ring of golden engraved cloud motifs around the disc. Cosmic and fluid.

A floating gilded armillary sphere (浑天仪) of interlocking golden rings at different angles, engraved with tiny star marks, enclosing a glowing pearl-like small sun at its centre that lights the rings from within; faint dragon-cloud swirls of golden mist around it. Ornate but with a bold readable round silhouette.

A celestial all-seeing eye: an almond eye shape made of two crescent moons in gold, the iris a deep swirling galaxy with a bright golden star as the pupil, golden rays fanning out behind it like a sunburst, a few constellation points scattered around. Mysterious, oracle-like, hypnotic.

A celestial phoenix (朱雀, the Vermilion Bird of the southern sky) whose body and spread wings are drawn as glowing golden constellation stars and flowing flame-feathers with cinnabar-red accents, encircling a full golden moon; wings form a strong symmetrical round silhouette. Epic, fantastical, elegant.
